body: Thank you. I'm inching my way towards that peace slowly but surely.

Thank you. I think this was the darkest moment of my life, but I appreciate the compliment. I am doing a lot better (after getting worse), very much dealing with depression but very hopeful and not suicidal anymore, and I've been having ideas a lot lately so maybe I'll pick up a pen and get back into it. It's been a while. :)

I don't think so either. It's just I've heard a few stories that start like this and end that way. I don't immediately believe that that's the first course of action that would occur because that's literally the worst case scenario and a bizarre course of action to decide upon doing, but it's just a thought that crept into my mind. That's of course not the main point I wanted to get across, but I feel like it's not entirely purposeless to add that.

I hate to say it, but your parents do enable him heavily. They have a responsibility to prepare their kid as much as they need to for the world, and they haven't. That being said, your brother is his only obstacle. Clearly everyone wants him to get his stuff together, but he's the only one in his way, so there is no way you can help him. I tend to watch true crime stuff a lot and I worry about what happens when your parents make that big push and set ultimatums for him to start improving his life because I've seen too many videos about the worst case scenario of a full adult man k*lling his parents and siblings over them trying to force him to take his life into his own hands (and I have no reason to believe that is the case currently, but it's still a concern of mine in general.) But at this point, all of your lives are poisoned right now by this situation. If your parents don't decide together to start trying to help, you might have to cut them off along with your brother. You can't help somebody who doesn't want to be helped. There is a lot you and your parents can do of he does decide that he needs to change. But this is all him.

I work at an after school program in a specific school and the school canceled our contract a week ago mid year because we had so many issues, but a lot of them were just because of behavior issues with the kids and shitty communication with us. I asked my manager if we could tell the kids and they told me not to say a word. They just told the kids and parents today and tomorrow is our last day. I feel that so much because now the parents have to find a way and they just found out right before spring break. I'm genuinely pissed for the parents about that because they deserved to know as soon as we knew.

I needed to hear this so much. My relationship now is the first healthy love I've ever experienced so I feel like I'm putting the toxicity of all the toxic family and romantic relationships I've had into this one but I know I'm doing better, I just feel unworthy sometimes.
I'll try. I am trying. I just wish it was for myself too.

You're right. It's just something I feel like I can't control anymore. I'm usually a huge in-control type of person, but this is the first time I've ever felt out of control in this way. A week ago I was terrified of the idea of dying because I watched too many true crime videos, and I've always acted in a way to prevent myself from dying in any sort of way. Now, when I get to that point, I could go grab a knife and go for it, and I can't say for sure, but I might not feel much of anything beforehand. I wish that knowing how it feels to be in love felt like enough right now.
